summary.text: Joseph Morelle is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent in NY-25, an Upstate New York native, former small-business owner and longtime local and state legislator. After serving on the Monroe County Legislature and in the New York State Assembly, where he was majority leader from 2013 to 2018, he won a 2018 special election to succeed the late Rep. Louise Slaughter. He is ranking member of the Committee on House Administration and serves on Appropriations.

paragraphs.text: Morelle was born in Oneida County, New York, and his congressional biography describes him as a lifelong resident of Upstate New York. He graduated from Eastridge High School and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the State University of New York at Geneseo in 1986.

He worked as an administrator at the Anthony L. Jordan Health Center and as president and CEO of MMI Technologies, Incorporated; his congressional biography calls him a former small business owner. Morelle was previously elected to the Monroe County Legislature, according to that biography.
He served in the New York State Assembly from 1991 to 2018, representing the 132nd District until 2013 and the 136th District from 2013 to 2018. He was Assembly Majority Leader from 2013 to 2018.

Morelle won the 2018 special election for New York's 25th District, which includes Monroe County and part of Ontario County, after the death of Rep. Louise Slaughter, and has represented the district since. In the 119th Congress he is ranking member of the Committee on House Administration and the Joint Committee on the Library, and he sits on the Appropriations Committee, with seats on its Defense and Commerce, Justice, Science subcommittees.
His office says he lives in Irondequoit with his wife, Mary Beth; they have three children and five grandchildren.
